summary.headline: Aarti Drugs Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue hit a record Rs 829 crore (+27% YoY) and EBITDA margin rose to 16.6% (+370 bps).
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was a record quarter: consolidated revenue of Rs 829 crore grew 27% YoY, EBITDA rose 63% to Rs 138 crore and PAT rose 83% to Rs 83 crore. Growth was driven mainly by price (API realisations up about 16-18% YoY) rather than volume (about 5% in Q2 and 3% in Q1). Formulations subsidiary Pinnacle grew 58% on exports, which management called exceptional, and it currently has about four months of export orders. Management guided that a consolidated EBITDA margin of about 15% is sustainable, while acknowledging Q2 was 16.6%.

financial_highlights.change: +83% YoY from Rs 45 crore; PAT margin 10.0% (+310 bps)
+48% YoY from Rs 159 crore; margin 15.3% (+250 bps)
+34% YoY from Rs 99 crore; margin 8.7% (+70 bps)
+22% YoY from Rs 579 crore; 86% of consolidated revenue (corrected from 84% stated on call)
+58% YoY from Rs 83 crore; exports 74% of formulation revenue

segments.name: API (standalone, largest segment)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 605 crore in Q2 FY27 vs Rs 516 crore (+17%). Price growth about 17-18% YoY and volume about 5% for API plus specialty chemicals combined. Antibiotic category 34.1% of API sales, anti-diabetic 18.2%, anti-protozoal 18.1%, anti-inflammatory 14.8%, anti-fungal 9.3%.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 72 crore vs Rs 37 crore (+92%), supported by the Saykha methylamines facility, which ran at about 72% utilisation in the quarter.

segments.name: Formulations (Pinnacle Life Science)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 130 crore (+58%), led by exports (+73%). Management said Q2 formulation EBITDA margin was about 28%, and that 20% is a conservative steady-state level.

segments.name: Standalone export vs domestic
segments.commentary: Standalone domestic revenue grew 43% YoY and exports fell 5% YoY; the split was 68% domestic and 32% export.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA margin of around 15% seen as sustainable, though Q2 was 16.6%.
Standalone EBITDA margin has been above 14% for the last two quarters, with scope to improve further.
Formulation revenue expected to stay at the Q2 level for the rest of the year; formulation margin could fall to about 20% in the long term.
Original FY27 target of about 10% volume growth cut: management now assumes 5-10% volume growth for H2, with high single digits possible if customer demand returns.
Formulation business aspiration of Rs 1,000 crore may be reached earlier than previously published, once the Baddi expansion (due by mid-next year) and oncology ramp-up are in place.
Oncology share of revenue targeted at late 30s to early 40s percent by FY30 (per management estimate).
capex_capacity: Saykha methylamines plant commissioned September 2025, running at about 72% utilisation; captive consumption for anti-diabetic portfolio rose to about 85%.

Tarapur: started producing technical grade methyl salicylate, about 85 tonnes in the quarter; adjacent USFDA block being built to more than double capacity, with three multipurpose plants, 18-20 month build, commercial production targeted by end FY29. Potential revenue Rs 180-200 crore at full scale.

Sarigam: metformin capacity rising from 1,400 to 1,700 tonnes per month, commercialisation planned early FY28; dedicated 500 tonnes per month USFDA-compliant block by end FY28; metformin USFDA DMF under preparation.
Baddi (Himachal Pradesh): brownfield expansion on an adjacent plot to nearly double oral solid dosage capacity, expected by mid-next year.
Planned capex: CDMO block for intermediates and specialty chemicals, plus heavier R&D spend in formulations. Management expects clarity on capex for the 5-7 year plan within 4-5 months.
Solar projects expected to contribute from the December 2026 quarter.
demand_pricing: Developments in West Asia kept API prices firm; customers prioritised uninterrupted supply. Management said pricing currently stable, with crude-linked products the next driver of price growth.
Export order book about 2.5-3 months; domestic order book under one month. New contracts reprice quickly; pending orders are supplied at older, lower rates.
Raw material inventory held for about 40-50 days. Management does not plan to build extra raw material stock because high prices make it risky.
Formulation buyers are holding back stock purchases after the price spike, which slowed API volume growth.

Oncology: one US product recently launched with small Q2 contribution; another ANDA due for approval in the next few months; filings planned for four to five more oncology products over rolling 12 months.
Salicylic acid anti-dumping duty: management expects DGTR initiation before December 2026, then a further three to six months before Finance Ministry action.

qa_highlights.question: How much of API growth is price vs volume, and does the H1 split match?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 API price growth was about 17-18% YoY and combined API plus specialty chemicals volume growth about 5%. Q1 volume growth was about 3% and rate growth 16-17%; H1 rate variance about 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the formulation growth a one-off, and is the 15% margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Formulation growth is from new export markets and products under registration; management called Q2 exceptional but expects similar revenue to be sustained. Consolidated margin of about 15% is sustainable, with the caveat that gross margin falls as the cost-plus price base rises while overhead absorption improves.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide 15% when Q2 was 16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was being conservative. Formulation margin was about 28% in Q2, and even at a 20% formulation margin with standalone at 14%, consolidated margin would stay slightly above 15%.

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth is expected in H2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Original target was about 10% volume growth; H1 achieved 3% and 5%. Management now assumes 5-10% for the rest of the year, with high single digits possible if customers see the price rise as a new normal.

qa_highlights.question: Can formulation reach Rs 1,000 crore sooner, and what is the oncology timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes Rs 1,000 crore can come earlier than published. Baddi expansion is due by mid-next year, and oncology revenue is expected to rise in the next 3-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: How quickly are price increases passed on, and how much of Q2 gain is from peak-price contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: New orders reprice quickly; pending export orders (2.5-3 months) carry older prices. Management could not quantify the split because of the large product range.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the margin gain is from mix, efficiency and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: For standalone, about 50 bps came from higher gross contribution and the rest from lower manufacturing cost (energy and process optimisation). Formulation margin gain is mainly gross contribution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27 and FY28, given strong cash generation?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 operating cash flow was about Rs 90 crore, split roughly equally between standalone and formulations. Planned spend: the Tarapur USFDA block, the Sarigam metformin expansion, a CDMO block, and formulation R&D.

risks_watch: Sustainability of the 28% formulation margin in Q2; management now sees about 20% as a steady-state level.
API volume growth: H1 was 3-5% against an original target of about 10%, with customers holding back purchases.
Price pass-through lag on pending export orders (2.5-3 months) if input prices fall, given raw materials are held for 40-50 days.
Oncology US revenue is still small and ramp-up depends on the next ANDA approval and launches.
Salicylic acid anti-dumping duty timing: DGTR initiation expected by December 2026, with a further 3-6 months before Finance Ministry action.
Commissioning timelines: Sarigam metformin expansion (early FY28), Tarapur block (end FY29), Baddi expansion (mid next year).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and the expansion pipeline, but deliberately conservative on forward margin and volume guidance. Management was candid that H2 volume recovery depends on customer demand returning, and gave no numerical split for price pass-through.
key_quotes: These gains in product mix, backward integration and cost efficiency are structural and they will stay with us even as the pricing environment normalizes over time.
So, overall company margins, we do feel that 15% should be sustainable, though for this particular quarter, we have achieved EBITDA margins of around 16.6%.
So, we will assume somewhere between 5% to 10% volume growth.
So, we expect that in the coming three to six months, the US revenue would increase with the one product that we have in the market.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Formulation margin may fall from 28% to about 20%, pending export orders priced at older lower rates reprice down if input prices fall, and H2 volume depends on customers restarting purchases after the price spike.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: One US oncology product recently launched with small Q2 contribution, another ANDA due for approval in the next few months, and filings planned for four to five more oncology products over rolling 12 months.

rows.label: API price pass-through on new contracts
rows.why: API realisations up about 16-18% YoY in Q2, new orders reprice quickly while export order book of 2.5-3 months and domestic under one month carry older lower rates, so the pass-through lag supports the margin for one to two quarters.

rows.label: Salicylic acid anti-dumping duty

rows.label: Pinnacle export growth
rows.why: Formulation exports rose 73% in Q2 and Pinnacle has about four months of export orders, with management expecting Q2 formulation revenue (Rs 130 crore) to be sustained for the rest of the year.
